episodes.description: Why do traffic jams appear when there's no accident? In a 2008 experiment, 22 cars driving in a circle formed a stop-and-go jam all by themselves. Here's how one small tap of the brakes grows into a wave that travels backwards, and how one smooth driver can calm it.

episodes.description: Why can't you see your blind spot? Each of your eyes has an area where it sees nothing, because the optic nerve leaves the eye there and there are no light sensors. Here's how your other eye and your brain cover the gap, and how to find yours: cover your left eye, look at a cross, lean in, and watch a red dot vanish.
episodes.caption: There's a hole in your vision you've never noticed. Here's why, in clay.
